issue.title: ENV Variable not substituted
issue.body:
**Describe the bug**
When I build in local with `mvn package` and run the following command:
`export MP_OPENAPI_SERVERS=https://prod.server; java -jar target/app-1.0.0-SNAPSHOT-runner.jar`
My variable `mp.openapi.servers` is replaced.

When I do the same in a docker container from `maven:3.6.1-jdk-11-slim`
The variable in the Swagger is not replaced.

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
```
mvn io.quarkus:quarkus-maven-plugin:0.22.0:create \
    -DprojectGroupId=org.acme \
    -DprojectArtifactId=using-openapi-swaggerui \
    -DclassName="org.acme.openapi.swaggerui.FruitResource" \
    -Dpath="/fruits" \
    -Dextensions="resteasy-jsonb"

cd using-openapi-swaggerui/
./mvnw quarkus:add-extension -Dextensions="openapi"
./mvnw clean package -DskipTests
export MP_OPENAPI_SERVERS=https://test; java -jar target/using-openapi-swaggerui-1.0-SNAPSHOT-runner.jar

curl http://localhost:8080/openapi | grep servers -A1
```
You should see `https://test`

Now create a Dockerfile:
```
FROM quay.io/quarkus/centos-quarkus-maven:19.1.1 AS builder
COPY src /usr/src/app/src
COPY pom.xml /usr/src/app
USER root
RUN chown -R quarkus /usr/src/app
USER quarkus
RUN mvn -f /usr/src/app/pom.xml -DskipTests clean package

FROM fabric8/java-alpine-openjdk8-jre

COPY --from=builder /usr/src/app/target/lib/* /deployments/lib/
COPY --from=builder /usr/src/app/target/*-runner.jar /deployments/app.jar
ENTRYPOINT [ "/deployments/run-java.sh" ]
```
Then run:
```
docker run -e MP_OPENAPI_SERVERS=https://test -p 8080:8080 -it test
curl http://localhost:8080/openapi | grep servers -A1
```
The variable is not replaced

**Environment (please complete the following information):**

   - Local: `Darwin laptop799094.local 18.6.0 Darwin Kernel Version 18.6.0: Thu Apr 25 23:16:27 PDT 2019; root:xnu-4903.261.4~2/RELEASE_X86_64 x86_64`

 - Output of `java -version`:


body:
I tried the general idea with the a modified version of the `application-configuration` [quickstart](https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus-quickstarts/tree/master/application-configuration) (basically setting the value `greeting.message` to `${ENV_GREETING:hello}`) and things worked as expected.
I remember this working because I had added a SO [answer](https://stackoverflow.com/a/55806466/2504224) about it.

Then I also tried with the REST-Client and indeed I could reproduce the problem you mention.

@dmlloyd I looks like the `ExpandingConfigSource` is not used at runtime so when an attempt is made to pull a property value from `Config`, it never gets expanded.
Is there any reason we can't use `ExpandingConfigSource` for the in-jar properties?

> @dmlloyd I looks like the `ExpandingConfigSource` is not used at runtime so when an attempt is made to pull a property value from `Config`, it never gets expanded.

If not it's a bug.  We definitely should be adding the expander to all config sources.

That said it might not be worth fixing right now because (apart from the config work I'm already doing which would definitely conflict) I expect MP-config and thus SmallRye Config to formally support property expansion sometime in the next few weeks.
Nice! I think then it makes sense to wait.

I can't wait because of an important project. I need at least a workaround. I tried to place an application.properties in the config directory under the workdir but it is not working also. Any alternatives?
You can place `application.properties` in a directory named `config` which resides in the directory where you launch the process. Would that cover your needs temporarily?
@geoand I already tried that... sadly doesn't work..

@HeavyTobi doesn't work how? I have done that multiple times and it does work:

For example if I have:

```
/deployments/some-app.jar
/deployments/config/application.properties
```

and I launch the application from inside `/deployments` like so:

```
java -jar some-app.jar
```

then the (runtime) properties defined in `config/application.properties` will override the values of the `application.properties` file that is included inside the jar.
